51287100.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to influenza A virus hemagglutin by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: In order to further identify HA as the potential target, we then characterized the affinity between HA protein and the lead compound 14 by a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. We found that there was a strong binding affinity between HA protein and compound 14, with Kd values of 0.44 μM (Fig. 5). Notably, compound 14 displayed more potent binding with HA1 subunit compared to HA protein, with Kd values of 1.22 nM. Thus, we inferred that HA1 domain was the potential target on account of the high affinity between HA1 and the lead compound 14.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Fig.5. Interaction of compound 14 with HA (A) or HA1 (B) subunit detected by SPR.

original_paragraph.Figure 5 B: SPR Response (R.U.) vs Time (sec) for compound 14 with HA1. Concentrations: 60 nM (black), 120 nM (red), 240 nM (green), 480 nM (blue), 960 nM (cyan).
